candidate_rule_if_true: Rows with the same requested physical hold should land in the same latency phase.
fresh_counterexample: At requested 50ms, page.keyboard is tap-like at 250ms (0.0ms versus tap), while locator.type is slow (3.4ms) and locator.press(noWaitAfter) is also slow (3.4ms).
current_answer: Rejected as a global predictor. Hold duration is meaningful only inside an API family.
best_next_control: Interleave hold durations within each API/delay if the product question requires a best short-hold value.

candidate_rule_if_true: Rows with similar realized keydown-to-keyup duration should land in the same latency phase.
fresh_counterexample: page.keyboard 50ms is tap-like even though it realizes 97.7ms, while locator.type 75ms is slow at a nearby 93.5ms. locator.press 100ms is tap-like at 114.3ms.
current_answer: Rejected as a single threshold. The same observed-hold band contains tap-like, mixed, and slow rows.
best_next_control: Do not tune a universal physical-hold threshold from these data.

candidate_rule_if_true: Rows with the same configured wait after keyup should land in the same latency phase.
fresh_counterexample: At delay 500ms and requested hold 50ms, page.keyboard and locator.type both have a configured 450.0ms post-keyup wait; page.keyboard is -0.4ms versus tap, while locator.type is 2.8ms.
current_answer: Rejected. Ordinary waiting after keyup is not enough to predict the phase.
best_next_control: Further post-keyup work should focus on browser/runtime checkpoints rather than elapsed wait time.

candidate_rule_if_true: The shared low-level keyboard.press routine should determine the phase.
fresh_counterexample: locator.type and locator.press(noWaitAfter) both use keyboard.press internally and match at 50ms/75ms, but ordinary locator.press uses the same routine plus the press epilogue and stays tap-like: at 75ms/500ms, noWaitAfter is 3.1ms versus tap, while ordinary press is -1.2ms.
current_answer: Partly rejected. The key routine matters less than the automation work around it.
best_next_control: Use ordinary locator.press only as a checkpoint control, not as a model of pressSequentially/type.

candidate_predictor: locator focus/check path without press epilogue
candidate_rule_if_true: Per-key locator focus/checks, when not followed by the press epilogue, should behave like locator.type.
fresh_counterexample: This is the best current local rule: locator.type and locator.press(noWaitAfter) are within 0.0ms at 75ms/1000ms and within 0.1ms at 50ms/250ms.
current_answer: Supported for 50ms/75ms. It does not explain page.keyboard's separate 75ms/100ms slow band.
best_next_control: Run page.keyboard with a per-key locator.focus/evaluate checkpoint, and run page.keyboard.press({ delay }) plus post-keyup wait, to split focus/check work from explicit down/up timing.

candidate_rule_if_true: The press epilogue should move locator.press away from the locator.type/noWaitAfter band.
fresh_counterexample: At 50ms, removing the epilogue raises ordinary locator.press by a median 3.4ms in round-paired q50s; at 75ms the paired median is 3.9ms.
current_answer: Supported. This closes why ordinary locator.press is not a valid pressSequentially/type proxy.
best_next_control: No further local run needed unless Playwright changes this implementation.

candidate_rule_if_true: Later runs should all move in the same direction if machine drift explains the matrix.
fresh_counterexample: Ordinary locator.press ran late and returned to tap-like, then the clean noWaitAfter sequence ran later and moved 50ms/75ms back into the slow locator.type band.
current_answer: Rejected as the primary explanation for the API split.
best_next_control: Only repeat if absolute p50s, rather than the API-family sign, become the decision variable.
